reason: The single cited passage (E1) directly supports the core premises of nanoclustering-induced cohesion loss, intergranular cracking, and the proposed mitigation strategy, but the hypothesis overstates the evidence by claiming generality and a specific short-range order mechanism not explicitly established in the cited work.
premises: Nanoclustering of Cr, Ni, and Mn at grain boundaries reduces grain-boundary cohesion in CrMnFeCoNi.
This reduced cohesion promotes intergranular cracking and ductility/toughness loss.
Controlling segregation via heat treatment or Cr-rich secondary phases can preserve toughness.
The mechanism operates through local chemical short-range order at grain boundaries.
The phenomenon is common in single-phase fcc HEAs.
